items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Topics 39:1
items.html: It is known that the level of Bina divided into two Partzufim — GAR and the seven lower Sefirot, into Bina and Tvuna. The reason is the impression of the bottom Hey in the screen of the Rosh [head] of AA beneath Mocha Stimaa, which brought Bina outside. It governs only the seven lower Sefirot of Bina, since they require the illumination of Hochma, and it does not govern the GAR of Bina at all, since they are in covered Hassadim, which reject Hochma in any case. Therefore Bina and Tvuna became two distinct Partzufim: Bina is still in the discernment of GAR, whereas Tvuna went out from the discernment of GAR to the discernment of seven lower Sefirot lacking a Rosh. And it is discerned that they divided into fifty and fifty. For the complete level of Bina is one hundred Sefirot, being ten Sefirot each included in the other, and ten times ten are one hundred. However, now that they have divided, there remains in Tvuna only seven lower Sefirot included in one another — that is, seven Sefirot, in each of which are seven Sefirot, and seven times seven are forty-nine, that is, fifty less one. This indicates that they lack their Rosh and their GAR, which is called Keter, meaning the entire upper half of the Partzuf, called Bina, which divided off from above them and became a Partzuf of its own, as above. For this reason they are designated the forty-nine gates of Bina, one less than fifty. However, remember that this one gate means all fifty upper gates of the upper Bina, for this gate is the secret of Keter, whose meaning is Rosh and GAR. Yet the upper Bina too is likewise not complete so long as Tvuna is not joined with her and they become one Partzuf. She too is reckoned as lacking her upper gate, which is Keter and GAR. The reason is the known one, that a lack of the NHY of the vessels causes a lack of GAR in the lights. For in truth the GAR of Bina also went out from the Rosh of AA to the discernment of Garon [throat] and Guf [body]; only, since she is in the secret of “for He delights in mercy,” no matter of restriction applies to her, as above. Nevertheless, when reckoned with respect to the bestowal of Hochma, she too lacks GAR just like Tvuna. Thus, with respect to herself she is discerned as a complete Rosh, but with respect to Abba, who is Hochma, Bina too is considered to be seven lower Sefirot lacking a Rosh, since she cannot receive or impart Hochma, by force of the impression of the bottom Hey that remained in the screen of the Rosh of AA, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Topics 39:2
items.html: It follows that Bina too lacks GAR relative to Abba. Yet Bina is not on this account considered to be forty-nine gates as Tvuna is, for forty-nine gates indicates that there is in her herself only seven lower Sefirot, that is, seven times seven, as above — which is true only of Tvuna. But Bina, at any rate relative to herself, is a complete Rosh and does not lack GAR, as above. Rather, there is another discernment here, and it is in the discernment of the name MB in the simple form, the filling, and the filling of the filling, which indicates what they receive from the discernment corresponding to them in the three first Partzufim of AK, up to his Tabur, as above in answer 125. And it is known that the Partzufim of AK are the discernment of Hochma; therefore, by this reckoning, Bina is discerned as lacking the upper forty-second gate, that is, the discernment of the GAR of Hochma, which is called Rosh or Keter. For from the side of Hochma she has only forty-one gates and lacks the upper gate, that is, her Keter. For this gate is included in Abba, in the secret of the verse “Even (Gam) the bird has found a house,” and so forth. For the upper gate that Bina lacks was added to Abba, and Abba has forty-three gates, which is the secret of Gam [43].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Topics 39:3
items.html: And with this you will understand what the ARI wrote, that Moses merited Bina (above, Page 899, Item 52); and our sages said, fifty gates of Bina were created in the world, and all of them were given to Moses less one (Tractate Rosh Hashanah, page 21). It follows that he did not merit Bina in her completeness. And by the above you will understand this. For Moses merited the upper Bina in the secret of the forty-one gates in her — that is, so long as Bina and Tvuna are divided into two Partzufim, when they are reckoned as lacking their upper half, which is designated the discernment of their Keter: for Bina lacks the forty-second gate, and Tvuna lacks the fiftieth gate, as above. And to this our sages alluded when they said that all of them were given to Moses less one, that is, the fiftieth gate. For the fiftieth gate is the upper Bina, and she will not be permanently joined with Bina into one Partzuf until the end of correction, and therefore Moses did not merit her. And the ARI is speaking of the upper Bina when she is separated from the lower Tvuna, and it is this Bina that Moses merited — which likewise lacks one, namely the forty-second gate. (Page 963, Item 16).
